messages:
maria: Quick: candidate accepted, start date 12/29. Team wants to know whether the company shutdown (12/24-1/1) will require them to use PTO for 12/29-12/31 or if those are paid holiday days. Also curious if starting that late affects next-year carryover.
ton y: If theyre on payroll before shutdown start they get paid company holidays. Starting 12/29 = after shutdown start, so they wont get paid holiday days that ran earlier, but payroll rules vary for the tail end days.
hr-bot: POLICY CLIP: "Company shutdown days are paid to employees who are on payroll on the first day of the shutdown. New hires who start after the shutdown start are not automatically paid the earlier shutdown days and must use PTO if they want those dates off. Carryover eligibility is based on being active on 12/31."
maria: So because 12/29 is inside the shutdown window we need to clarify whether payroll treats them as active on 12/31. They will be on payroll by then, yes.
alan: If hire is active on 12/31 they are eligible for carryover next year (within cap). For shutdown pay: payroll calculates holiday pay based on active status on shutdown start. Since hire is after start, they won't get the full shutdown pay automatically.
payroll-bot: FYI: For hires who join during a shutdown, payroll will: 1) pay for shutdown days only if hire_date <= shutdown_start_date, 2) otherwise treat those dates as non-worked days. Managers must approve PTO if employee requests time off during shutdown.
maria: Managers prefer not to make new hires burn PTO during onboarding week. Any exceptions?
ton y: People Ops can approve one-time onboarding carve-outs in specific cases (customer-facing roles, critical start tasks). We require manager justification and a runbook checkbox at offer stage to auto-tag payroll.
alan: Suggest process: add "shutdown carve-out" checkbox to hiring checklist. If checked and People Ops approves, payroll will credit a one-time paid holiday mapping for the remaining shutdown days in the hires first pay cycle.
maria: Good. Also asked about unused PTO carryover: confirm that starting 12/29 and remaining employed through 12/31 means normal carryover eligibility.
hr-bot: CONFIRM: "Employees on payroll on 12/31 are eligible for standard carryover up to the published cap. No special blackout effect on eligibility."
maria: I'll add a sentence to the offer template: "If your start date falls within the company holiday shutdown, holiday pay and PTO treatment will follow payroll policy; managers may request a one-time onboarding carve-out via People Ops." Will tag legal if needed.
ton y: Thanks. If you want the auto-tag flow, fill the hire checklist and cc payroll. Closing loop. :white_check_mark:
